 Friday The 13th 2026: Know The Lore And Superstitions Behind The Unlucky Day
 The phobia of Friday the 13th has got two clinical names, paraskevidekatriaphobia and friggatriskaidekaphobia, and both are as hard to say as to explain.
 By   Mashable News Staff   
  Nov. 12, 2026 
 >
 Culture
 Friday the 13th arrives this November 13, the last such date of 2026 after February and March. The day has a reputation that has outlived most explanations for it. Some people avoid travel, put off signing contracts, or stay just home. The phobia of the day has two clinical names attached to it, namely, paraskevidekatriaphobia and friggatriskaidekaphobia, both as hard to pronounce as to explain. A cool pub trivia you should know about Friday the 13th is that every year has at least one Friday the 13th, and none has more than three. Tomorrow, Friday the 13th, will be the third this year we have had, and hopefully more fun.
 Friday the 13th: The Lore
 There are several lores associated with the Friday the 13th superstition. One of them is the Norse myth. Loki gatecrashed a dinner of 12 gods as the uninvited 13th guest, which got Baldur killed due to his mischief. Per some Orthodox Christian tradition, 13 people gathered at the Last Supper, with Judas the last to sit, and the crucifixion occurred on a Friday. In some accounts, October 13, 1307, a Friday, was when France's King Philip IV had the Knights Templar arrested. However, none of the aforementioned traditions are seen as historically the origin of the phobia for the Friday the 13th date.
 Friday the 13th: In Pop Culture
 Plenty of hotels and hospitals still skip a 13th floor or room number. No one knows exactly why. Some say the number is unlucky or associated with the devil himself. Thomas W. Lawson's 1907 novel " Friday, the Thirteent h" follows a broker who uses this superstition to crash the stock market. Renowned Italian composer Gioachino Rossini died on Friday, November 13, 1868, and is said to have dreaded the date. He was born on February 29, 1792, a strange leap year date! The 1980 slasher film "Friday the 13th" gave the world Jason Voorhees, and the day has never been the same again.

 When Is The Next Friday the 13th?
 The next Friday the 13th falls on August 13, 2027.
 BTW, did you know November 13, 2015, was also a Friday? The day marked a bloodbath across Paris, as terrorists attacked the city with suicide bombers, leaving at least 130 people dead, which included 90 at the Batacian Theater.
